subject.title: Terminal-main reconciliation gate silently resets a healthy main session when a post-run transcript append lands after updatedAt (mtime race)

question: Should terminal-main reconciliation remain allowed to override a configured fresh reset policy, or must it use a stronger authoritative divergence signal before rolling over the session?
rationale: The existing behavior deliberately favors recovery from stale terminal rows, while the reported false-positive path silently discards active context; choosing the permanent precedence and evidence signal changes a user-visible session recovery policy.

options.title: Use authoritative divergence
options.body: Preserve stale-row recovery but replace raw mtime comparison with a writer-owned mutation marker or semantic transcript cursor.

options.title: Require policy staleness
options.body: Apply transcript reconciliation only after the configured daily or idle policy is stale, accepting weaker recovery for fresh wedged rows.

options.title: Keep current gate
options.body: Retain mtime-based fail-closed rollover and require concrete proof of an unsupported or missing-marker transcript writer before changing behavior.

recommendation.title: Use authoritative divergence
recommendation.body: Preserve stale-row recovery but replace raw mtime comparison with a writer-owned mutation marker or semantic transcript cursor.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad ownership of session rollover and expiry invariants, including the surrounding admission module and related behavior tradeoffs.
